name: skeleton

test_list.description: Rust fn/struct/trait/impl signatures are kept, bodies (and the marker inside them) are gone; methods are depth 1.
An item's span covers the full declaration including its body.
Tuple/unit structs, enums, modules, const, static, type aliases, macros, async/unsafe/generic fns and trait impls.
Python class with decorated and async methods plus a top-level def; the span of a decorated class keeps its decorators.
__global__, __device__ __forceinline__ and template prefixes stay in the signature; the <<<>>> launch is not part of it.
C++ namespaces, classes, struct, constructors, destructors, pure virtuals, inline methods, prototypes and qualified definitions.
Exports, interfaces, classes with constructor/async methods, arrow-function consts, type aliases, enums and namespaces.
A file with a syntax error still yields the declarations tree-sitter recovered.
Whitespace runs inside a signature collapse to single spaces.
A signature above MAX_SIGNATURE_BYTES is truncated at a char boundary and ends with an ellipsis.
3000 nested modules are walked iteratively with correct depths.
More than MAX_SKELETON_ITEMS items returns TooLarge.
An empty source yields no items in every language.
Property: item spans are ordered, in bounds and on char boundaries.
Property: identifiers that occur only inside a body never appear in the rendered skeleton.

output_description: Signature-only items in source order with kind, name, collapsed signature, span and nesting depth.
